subject: 00BA6D4E6EF645E480AB0B732786C2BB
introduction: What is a Messenger of God in relation to God? The readings answer with a mirror. The sun is seen in it entire, so that the mirror may truly say, the sun is in me; and the sun has not left its place. From this they draw two statements that must both stand. A Manifestation who says “I am God” speaks the truth, since nothing is seen in Him but God’s attributes, and one who says “I am but a servant” speaks it equally, since the Essence is beyond all incarnation and all likeness. Whoever knows Him has known God, and He is His own first proof. The same tension runs through John’s Gospel, where Jesus says both “I and my Father are one” and “my Father is greater than I”, and through the Qur’an on its Prophet. Christian doctrine resolved it differently, and the Nicene Creed, the Word made flesh and the fulness of the Godhead bodily are set here as contrasts, with the apostles’ refusal of divine honours and the objections of Locke and Paine to a proof that only its bearer can give.
questions: The readings hold that a Manifestation may truly say both “I am God” and “I am a servant”. How does the picture of the mirror make room for both?
John’s Gospel has Jesus say that he and the Father are one, and that the Father is greater than he. How have you understood those two sayings together?
The Word was made flesh, says John; the Unseen can in no wise incarnate His Essence, say the readings. Where exactly is the difference, and what does each side wish to protect?
The Qur’an insists that its Prophet is a mortal and but a messenger, and also that to obey him is to obey God. What does that combination guard against?
Emerson thought everyone may say “I am divine”. What do the readings reserve to the Manifestation, and what do they give to everyone?
The Manifestation is said to be His own proof, as the sun is. What does that mean for someone who was not there, and has only the record?

outside.why: These are the words the reading interprets: he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.
John's Gospel says in its first chapter that no one has seen God at any time; the Son has declared Him.
Jesus says: I can of mine own self do nothing; I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father.
John the Baptist put the same self-effacement in a sentence: he must increase, but I must decrease.
When a man called him Good Master, Jesus answered: why callest thou me good? There is none good but one, that is, God.
The Qur’an has Muhammad say: I am only a mortal like you; my Lord inspires in me that your God is One.
The Qur’an says of an act of the Prophet: thou threwest not when thou didst throw, but God threw.
Jesus said: before Abraham was, I am, and his hearers understood whose words he was using.
The same Gospel has him say: my Father is greater than I.
In Revelation a voice says: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending.
Paul's hymn says that he took upon him the form of a servant and humbled himself.
God says to Moses in Exodus: see, I have made thee a god to Pharaoh.

When Jesus said, I and my Father are one, his hearers took up stones, saying that he, being a man, made himself God. What would make such a declaration true on one man's lips and blasphemy on another's?

The Qur’an says that it is not possible for one to whom God gave scripture and prophethood to say to people: be servants of me instead of God. How does the reading keep the words I am God from meaning what this verse forbids?

The Council of Nicaea settled on the phrase of one substance with the Father. Does the reading's double statement, I am God and I am His servant, say the same thing by another road, or something different?
Jesus answered the charge of blasphemy by quoting a psalm: I said, ye are gods, to whom the word of God came. What is the difference between that sense of the word and the sense in this reading?
Jesus says: my doctrine is not mine, but His that sent me.
John's Gospel says that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us. How do Christians who hold the incarnation and readers of this passage each understand what was seen in Jesus?
The Qur’an says that the Messiah was no other than a messenger, like the messengers who passed away before him.
Paul calls Christ the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature.
The first letter to Timothy says that there is one God, and one mediator between God and men.
In Exodus the voice comes to Moses out of the midst of a bush that burns and is not consumed.
The Letter to the Hebrews calls the Son the brightness of God's glory and the express image of His person.
Israel's confession guards the same point: the Lord our God is one Lord.
The Qur’an tells the people of the scripture: say not Three; God is only one God.
Jesus says that the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he sees the Father do.
God says of the prophet to come: I will put my words in his mouth, and he shall speak all that I command him.
Jeremiah tells how the Lord touched his mouth and said: behold, I have put my words in thy mouth.
John's Gospel speaks of the true Light, which lights every person coming into the world.
Isaiah says of the servant that he has no form nor comeliness, and no beauty that we should desire him.
Jesus says: I have not spoken of myself; the Father gave me a commandment what I should say.
Locke held that reason must be our last judge and guide in everything, revelation included. What is a believer doing with his reason when he accepts that a Messenger's every word is to be received?
Paul says that the light of the knowledge of God's glory is given in the face of Jesus Christ.
The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of a priest without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days nor end of life.
The people of Nazareth asked: is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary? What do those who know a Messenger's family and trade see, and what do they miss?
Krishna says in the Gita that the untaught mistake him, veiled in form, and see nothing of his nature.
Paul speaks of beholding the glory of the Lord as in a glass and being changed into the same image.
Jesus tells his disciples: he that receiveth me receiveth Him that sent me.
Krishna says that when righteousness declines he comes forth age after age. How does one manifestation in all the Prophets differ from one God descending many times?
Paul writes that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself.
Isaiah asks to whom God may be likened, and what likeness may be compared to Him.
Paul says of himself: I live, yet not I, but Christ liveth in me.
Jesus told his disciples that he had many things to say which they could not bear yet.
Emerson thought that what Jesus said of himself every person may say: I am divine; through me God acts. What is lost if the words He is I and I am He are taken for a truth about everyone?
The Letter to the Hebrews says that God spoke at sundry times and in divers manners by the prophets.
Rumi says that the lamps are different but the Light is the same: it comes from beyond.
The first letter of John finds love in the sending: herein is love, that He loved us and sent His Son.
Julian of Norwich asked what her Lord meant in all that she was shown, and was answered: love was his meaning.
Plotinus pictures what proceeds from the One as light around the sun, never cut off from it and never the same as it.
Augustine found a likeness of the three in love: the lover, the beloved, and the love. What does the picture of mirrors explain that his does not, and the reverse?

The first letter to Timothy calls it the mystery of godliness that God was manifest in the flesh. Is the distinction between the body of Jesus and the Christhood one that the New Testament itself makes?
Jesus says in John's Gospel, in the temple at the feast of dedication: I and my Father are one.
Jesus cried out: he that believeth on me believeth on Him that sent me, and he that seeth me seeth Him that sent me.
Plato uses the sun for the highest reality: it gives visibility and growth to what it shines on, and is neither of them.
Colossians says that in Christ dwells all the fulness of the Godhead bodily. How would you explain to a Christian friend what the readings affirm of Christ and what they decline to say?
Thomas, seeing the risen Jesus, said: my Lord and my God. Was his confession about essence or about what he saw in the one before him?
When God proclaims His name to Moses, what is proclaimed is a list of attributes: merciful, gracious, longsuffering.
One of Job's friends puts the question that has no answer: canst thou by searching find out God?
Jesus says: though I bear record of myself, my record is true, for I know whence I came.
Elsewhere in the same Gospel Jesus says: if I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. What kinds of testimony does a Messenger offer, and what kind does a hearer need?
Jesus asked his disciples what others said of him, and then: but whom say ye that I am?
The chief priests asked Jesus by what authority he did these things, and he would not tell them.
Three disciples saw his face shine as the sun on the mountain.
Thomas Paine argued that a revelation is revelation to the first person only, and hearsay to everyone after. How can the sun be its own proof for those who were not there to see it?
The people of his own town asked whence he had these things, and were offended at him.
The Qur’an states the same identity of response: whoso obeyeth the messenger hath obeyed God.
Jesus says in his prayer: this is life eternal, that they might know Thee, and Jesus Christ whom Thou hast sent.
Jesus warned that not everyone who says Lord, Lord shall enter the kingdom, but the one who does the will. How do recognition and conduct depend on each other?
Jesus said, leaving no middle ground: he that is not with me is against me.

When the people of Lystra called Paul and Barnabas gods, the apostles tore their clothes and said: we are men of like passions with you. Why do the same scriptures hold that claim to be right for one and wrong for others?
The Qur’an says that those who swear allegiance to the Prophet swear allegiance to God: the hand of God is above their hands.
Acts tells of a king who let a crowd say, It is the voice of a god and not of a man, and gave not God the glory.
The Qur’an says: Muhammad is but a messenger; messengers have passed away before him.

john-my-father-is-greater-than-i.text: Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I

john-of-mine-own-self-do-nothing.text: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me

john-before-abraham-was.text: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am

john-my-record-is-true.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go

john-if-i-bear-witness-of-myself.text: If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true

matthew-receiveth-him-that-sent-me.text: He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me

exodus-face-to-face.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend

john-my-doctrine-is-not-mine.text: Jesus answered them, and said, My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself

corinthians-god-was-in-christ.text: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation

john-ye-are-gods.text: Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God

acts-voice-of-a-god.text: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them. And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man. And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost

quran-thou-threwest-not.text: Ye (Muslims) slew them not, but Allah slew them. And thou (Muhammad) threwest not when thou didst throw, but Allah threw, that He might test the believers by a fair test from Him. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower.

quran-be-ye-faithful-servants.text: It is not (possible) for any human being unto whom Allah had given the Scripture and wisdom and the prophethood that he should afterwards have said unto mankind: Be slaves of me instead of Allah; but (what he said was): Be ye faithful servants of the Lord by virtue of your constant teaching of the Scripture and of your constant study thereof.
